title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] Can you explain: how do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

Here's the thing: You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: District Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[District Attorney races] How does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?

The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, emergency Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, emergency Funds] How do we handle fundraising for bail or legal defense?

This is where speed and trust matter most. Use encrypted channels to blast out the need to your most dedicated supporters the second a comrade is snatched. Keep these funds strictly segregated from your operating budget so that when the hammer drops, you can move instantly to get our people back on the streets where they belong.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: surveillance Awareness] Give me the short version: What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In-kind Donations
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In-kind Donations] A friend asked me: 'Someone wants to give us gear instead of cash. Is that helpful?' What do I tell them?

Hell yes, take the gear and put it to work immediately. If a comrade has a high-end printer, a PA system, or a van they aren't using, that's thousands of dollars we don't have to raise ourselves. Every physical asset we own is a tool for the struggle, so catalog it, maintain it, and make sure it's always ready for the next mobilization. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, transparent Treasuries] How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again.

title: Karl Organizing: Social pressure
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social pressure] How do we handle coworkers who are openly against the union?

Don't waste all your energy on the hardcore 'no' votes. Focus on the 'undecideds' and the 'soft yes' folks. For the ones who are actively sabotaging, let their own friends and coworkers talk to them. Social pressure from peers is way more effective than any argument you can make. If they want to be the boss's pet, let them explain that to the people they work with every day.

title: Karl Organizing: Clinic Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Clinic Defense] A friend asked me: 'What do I do if I see harassers blocking a healthcare clinic?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Show up with a group of comrades and use your bodies to create a physical corridor for patients to walk through safely. Wear bright vests so you're easily identified as the good guys and keep your backs to the harassers to avoid being baited into a shouting match. Your job isn't to debate bigots; it's to be a human shield for someone just trying to access care. Stay calm, stay focused, and keep the path clear.

title: Karl Organizing: Safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safe Zones] How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: Property Seizure
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Property Seizure] They took my backpack and my sign during the arrest. Can I get them back?

Here's the thing: Demand a voucher or a receipt for every single item they take from you during processing. If they refuse, make a mental note of the officer's badge and report it to the legal team as soon as you're out. We'll fight to get your gear back, but never let a lost bag stop you from getting back into the struggle.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: elderly Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: elderly Care] Give me the short version: How do we make sure the seniors in our building aren't being forgotten?

Do a door-knock every Sunday just to check in and see if they need help with groceries, light bulbs, or tech issues. Many of our elders are isolated by a society that only values people who are currently being exploited for profit. Listen to their stories—they've seen more than you and usually have the best advice for surviving the long haul. A simple check-in can be the difference between someone thriving or suffering in silence.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] A friend asked me: 'Should I make my accounts private?' What do I tell them?

Private accounts are a hurdle, not a wall. The platforms still own your data and will sell you out. If you’re an organizer, have a public-facing 'persona' for outreach and a completely locked-down, pseudonymous account for your real life. Use a different photo, a different name, and never link the two. Starve the algorithm of your real connections. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: using Voter Files
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: using Voter Files] Give me the short version: Do we really need expensive voter data software?

Data is just a map, but you're the one who has to walk the path. Use the basic public records to find out who hasn't been talked to in years—the renters, the young people, and the marginalized who the big parties ignore. Don't get bogged down in spreadsheets; use the information to target the doors where a conversation will have the most impact. Our strategy is to expand the electorate by engaging the people the system has abandoned.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, legal Observers] Who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?

Real talk: Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: Food distribution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food distribution] What's the best way to run a food distribution?

Partner with food banks for supply — they throw away mountains of good food. Pick a consistent time and place so people can rely on it. No ID, no questions, no sermons. Bag staples people actually cook with. And recruit from the community you're serving — the distribution should be run by neighbors, not outsiders.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, phone Security] Can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?

Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowdfunding Platforms] Can you explain: which website should we use to raise money online?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support.

title: Karl Organizing: Food Sourcing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Food Sourcing] A friend asked me: 'We have a fridge but it's always empty. Where do we get enough food to keep it full?' What do I tell them?

Real talk: Talk to the managers at local independent grocers and bakeries about their 'waste'—most of them hate throwing good food away but follow corporate rules. Organize a weekly grocery run where neighbors buy one extra staple item to drop off, and coordinate with local farms for their surplus harvests. We don't need charity; we need to redirect the abundance the capitalists are prepared to rot in a dumpster. Pool resources to buy in bulk when things are on sale.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] A friend asked me: 'What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?' What do I tell them?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Security for Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security for Funds] Can you explain: who should be in charge of the money?

Never leave the bag with just one person. Elect a committee of three people who have to sign off on any major spending and who are all accountable to the general membership. This prevents burnout, stops bad actors from disappearing with the loot, and ensures that every spending decision reflects the will of the collective.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, inclusivity in Action] How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, dispersal Orders] The police are telling us to leave or face arrest. Should we move?

Real talk: Listen closely to the order and decide right then if you're prepared for the inside of a cell today. If you're staying, link arms with your crew and brace yourself; if you're leaving, move in a tight, organized group toward the designated exit. Never run, because that's when the pigs start hunting individuals who get separated from the pack.

title: Karl Organizing: City Council motivation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[City Council motivation] Why should I run for city council when the real power is in DC?

The feds won't stop your landlord from hiking the rent, but a council vote can. We're seizing the levers that actually touch people’s lives every single morning—the cops, the zoning, and the water bills. Grab a clipboard, talk to the people at the bus stop, and let’s start making the bosses sweat where they actually live. Don't wait for a savior from the capital when you can be the shield for your own block right now.

title: Karl Organizing: Starting a Union
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Starting a Union] I want to organize my building, but I'm afraid of getting evicted. How do I start safely?

Fear is what the landlord trades in, comrade, but they can't evict an entire building at once. Start by talking to your most trusted neighbors one-on-one behind closed doors, never in the lobby where cameras are watching. Build a secret contact sheet and map out who lives where. Strength comes from the shadows first; by the time the parasite knows there's a union, you'll already have the numbers to make retaliation a PR nightmare for them. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Browser Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Browser Security] A friend asked me: 'Is Chrome okay if I use 'Incognito' mode?' What do I tell them?

Chrome is a spy tool built by a multi-billion dollar advertising company. Incognito mode only hides your history from your roommate, not from Google or the feds. Switch to Brave or Firefox with privacy extensions, or use Tor if you need real anonymity. We can't build a new world using the master's surveillance tools. Protect your browsing habits like your life depends on it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, spotting ICE
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, spotting ICE] What should I look for if I think ICE is in my neighborhood?

Look for unmarked white or dark SUVs with tinted windows lurking near apartment complexes at dawn. They often wear vests that just say POLICE in generic block letters to trick folks into opening their doors. If you see them, blast the location to your network immediately with a photo of the plates. We protect our neighbors by being the early warning system the feds can't hide from. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] What are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, legal Rights Training] What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

Here's how it works: The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct.

title: Karl Organizing: Night Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Night Safety] How can we keep the neighborhood safe at night without more patrols?

Organize 'walking school buses' or evening stroll groups so nobody has to walk alone if they don't want to. Fix broken streetlights ourselves or install motion-sensor lights in dim areas with the permission of the residents. Increasing positive foot traffic is the best way to discourage actual harm. We light up the dark with solidarity, not with police sirens. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Tenant union basics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Tenant union basics] How do I start a tenant union in my building?

Knock on doors. Seriously — start with your floor, then the building. Ask everyone the same question: what's broken, what does the landlord ignore? Collect it all. Then call a meeting — food helps, childcare helps more. Draft collective demands with a deadline. A tenant union isn't a legal entity you register; it's your neighbors deciding to act together. The landlord fears coordination, not complaints. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: district Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, small Group Value
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, small Group Value] Is it worth the time joining up with tiny local groups that only have five members?

A hundred pebbles make a landslide if you throw them at the same time. Those tiny groups have deep roots in their specific neighborhoods that your big city organization will never have. Respect their local knowledge, share your printing press and bullhorns, and build a front that the bosses can't ignore just by looking at a map. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Benefit event planning
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Benefit event planning] How do I throw a benefit show for the cause?

Book local bands who believe in it, find a donated venue, price tickets on a sliding scale. Sell merch and food. Keep the politics front and center — this isn't just a concert, it's a fundraiser with a purpose. Announce the total raised that night. Transparency builds trust, and trust builds the next event.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, escalation Management] What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed.

title: Karl Organizing: Rejecting Corporate Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rejecting Corporate Cash] Can you explain: a local real estate developer offered to sponsor our community garden. Take it?

Absolutely not. Those developers are the ones driving your neighbors out of their homes; taking their money is just helping them paint a smiley face on displacement. If they want to help the garden, they can stop hiking the rent. We'll fund our own soil and seeds through bake sales and tool-shares before we take a bribe from a landlord.

title: Karl Organizing: Membership Perks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Membership Perks] Do we need to give donors gifts like tote bags or stickers?

The best 'perk' you can give a comrade is a victory against the bosses. Don't waste money on trinkets that eat into your margins. Give them a vote in the organization, a seat at the strategy table, and the knowledge that they are part of a serious force for change; that's worth more than any canvas bag.

title: Karl Organizing: Quiet Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quiet Zones] Some people find protests overwhelming. How can we help them stay?

Set up a designated 'low-stim' area at the back of the march or at the rally site where people can take a breather away from the drums and megaphones. Have a couple of comrades stationed there with water and earplugs to help people ground themselves. Inclusion means making sure everyone, including neurodivergent comrades, has a way to contribute without hitting a breaking point.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] A friend asked me: 'Why should I bother with Signal when I have nothing to hide?' What do I tell them?

Privacy isn't about having secrets; it's about power. When you use unencrypted SMS, you're handing a transcript of your life to the state and the billionaire carriers. Use Signal for everything. Set your messages to disappear after five minutes so there's no paper trail for some ambitious prosecutor to use against your crew. We protect our own by leaving no tracks.

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinic Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinic Logistics] I want to start a free clinic, but none of us are doctors. Is it still possible?

You don't need a medical degree to run a first-aid station or a herbal medicine collective, so start where you are. Focus on preventative care, wound cleaning, and distributing naloxone to keep our people alive in the streets. Partner with sympathetic nurses or EMTs who are tired of the insurance industry's greed and want to actually help folks. We're building a parallel system of care because the private hospitals would rather see us die than see us broke.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, phone Hygiene] What's the best way to back up my phone before an action?

Back it up to a local hard drive at home, then encrypt that drive with a strong password. Turn off all auto-syncing to the cloud—Apple and Google will hand over your 'private' backups the moment the state asks. Once your backup is safe at home, wipe any sensitive messages or photos from the device you're carrying. Travel light and travel clean.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Undercovers] Can you explain: how can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Look, Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle.

title: Karl Organizing: Disaster Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Disaster Rapid Response] A storm just hit our town. What's the first move for a mutual aid group?

Get on the ground immediately and set up a hub with water, charging stations, and hot food before the red tape of the NGOs even arrives. Use a simple spreadsheet or a signal thread to track who needs a roof patched and who has a chainsaw to clear the roads. Don't wait for a government check that's never coming; check on your elderly neighbors and start clearing debris yourself. Solidarity is a verb, and it's loudest when the sirens are still going off.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with consultants
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with consultants] Who are these 'labor relations specialists' the company just hired?

Those are union-busting mercenaries paid thousands of dollars a day to lie to your face. Their only job is to spread fear, uncertainty, and doubt so you don't realize how much the boss is stealing from you. They get rich by keeping you poor. Tell your coworkers exactly what they're being paid and remind them that money could have gone into your paychecks instead.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, de-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, de-escalation] How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?

Real talk: Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: grant Alternatives] Give me the short version: Foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: building Trust] Give me the short version: How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Let me break it down: Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transparent Treasuries] Can you explain: how do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Here's the thing: Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: burner Devices] Give me the short version: Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: transit Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: transit Policy] Give me the short version: What's the radical approach to local transit?

Make it free and make it frequent. Public transit should be a service like the library or the fire department, funded by taxing the corporations that benefit from workers being able to get to their jobs. Fight for dedicated bus lanes and expanded routes that serve the neighborhoods the current system ignores. Mobility is a right, and we should be taking the streets back from private cars and giving them to the people.

title: Karl Organizing: Emergency Funds
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Emergency Funds] A friend asked me: 'How do we handle fundraising for bail or legal defense?' What do I tell them?

This is where speed and trust matter most. Use encrypted channels to blast out the need to your most dedicated supporters the second a comrade is snatched. Keep these funds strictly segregated from your operating budget so that when the hammer drops, you can move instantly to get our people back on the streets where they belong.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with police kettling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with police kettling] What do I do if police kettle a protest?

Stay calm, stay with your group, and document everything. Kettling is designed to panic people into running — don't. If you're detained, say your name and nothing else. Legal observers should be filming from outside the kettle. This is why you have a jail support number memorized and a buddy who knows you're there. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, resource Pooling] How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: resource Sharing] Give me the short version: How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Crowd Logistics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Crowd Logistics] Can you explain: how do we stay organized when things get chaotic in the street?

Look, Use the 'buddy system' so nobody is ever standing alone or getting snatched without a witness. Assign roles like 'scout,' 'vibe checker,' and 'legal' so everyone knows exactly what their job is when the pressure starts. If the group needs to move, do it together in a tight block rather than scattering. A disorganized crowd is a target; an organized community is a force.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, burner Devices] Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

Let me break it down: No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response] Can you explain: how do we mobilize the whole coalition quickly when something bad happens?

Here's how it works: Set up a phone tree or an encrypted signal blast that can reach every member in under ten minutes. You need a 'break glass in case of emergency' plan where everyone knows exactly which street corner to stand on when the cops show up or the layoffs start. Speed is our only advantage against the slow, bloated bureaucracy of the state and the corporations.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: small-Dollar Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: small-Dollar Strategy] Give me the short version: How do we fund the fight without taking corporate money?

We pool our resources because ten thousand workers giving five bucks is more powerful than one billionaire buying a candidate. Be honest with the people: tell them you're the only one in the race who doesn't answer to a developer or a lobbyist. When you ask folks to chip in, you're asking them to invest in their own collective power. Use that money for the essentials—flyers, stamps, and yard signs—and keep every receipt transparent to prove you're accountable to us, not them.

title: Karl Organizing: The Ask
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The Ask] A friend asked me: 'What's the best way to phrase a request for funds on social media?' What do I tell them?

Be direct, be urgent, and skip the flowery language. Tell them exactly what the crisis is, what we're doing to stop it, and exactly how much we need to get the job done. People want to be part of a winning fight, so show them that their five dollars is the literal fuel for the next victory.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: community Gardens
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: community Gardens] Give me the short version: The city says our neighborhood garden is illegal. Should we stop?

Keep planting and get the whole block to help you defend that dirt. Guerrilla gardening is an act of defiance against a system that wants us dependent on corporate grocery chains. If they try to bulldoze it, make sure there's a crowd there to stop them and a camera to record the state destroying a source of food. A plot of land that feeds people is more sacred than any zoning law written by a bureaucrat.
